summary: Embedded JWT in vendor DOCX triggered internal automation to provision temporary service accounts
description:
Issue summary:
A support engineer received an alert from the automation-queue consumer that a vendor DOCX uploaded to the partner intake bucket contained an embedded JSON Web Token (JWT). The ingest automation parsed the DOCX for metadata and inadvertently extracted the token which matched our internal automation matcher, triggering an automatic temporary service-account creation and granting of limited IAM roles.

Impact:
- One temporary service-account (sa-temp-0342) was auto-provisioned and used by downstream CI automation for ~7 minutes before flagged by monitoring.
- No sensitive data access logs observed beyond the automation's expected behavior (list and get on non-sensitive config buckets).
- Potential for an attacker to weaponize similar uploads to trigger unwanted provisioning.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (automation queue, ingest-service v3.2.7, iam-provisioner v1.8.0)
- Partner intake S3-like bucket: s3://partners-ingest-prod

Steps to reproduce (initial):
1) Vendor uploads DOCX to partners-ingest-prod via partner-form API.
2) ingest-service extracts text and looks for structured tokens per metadata matcher.
3) Extracted token matched automation rule: "provision-temporary-service-account" and invoked iam-provisioner.
4) iam-provisioner created sa-temp-0342 and attached role:iam.read-only-temp.

Observed evidence / logs:
- ingest-service log (2026-03-13T09:12:16Z): "extracted_metadata: {\"embedded\":true, \"payload_preview\":\"eyJhbGciOiJI...\" }"
- automation-queue trace id: aq-20260313-9a7c
- iam-provisioner audit (2026-03-13T09:12:22Z): "created serviceAccount sa-temp-0342 by automation-rule 'provision-temporary-service-account'"
- CloudTrail-like logs: role assignment and limited get/list calls from sa-temp-0342 from IP 18.215.42.33 (AWS AZ us-east-1a)

Immediate actions taken:
- Blocked automation rule "provision-temporary-service-account" (rolled to false) at 09:18:00Z.
- Rotated token/signing keys used by the ingest metadata matcher to prevent reuse.
- Revoked sa-temp-0342 and removed IAM bindings at 09:20:35Z.
- Snapshot of partner object (partners-ingest-prod/v2026-03-13/vendor-8923.docx) copied to investigator bucket for forensics.

Evidence artifacts location:
- investigator bucket: s3://sec-investigations/INT-612345/
- automation trace: aq-20260313-9a7c
- ingest-service logs: splunk://redwood/prod/ingest-service/2026-03-13
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-13T09:32:00Z: Raised after on-call alert. Attaching initial logs and object path. Requesting security triage.
Jordan Kim (Assignee) 2026-03-13T09:40:12Z: We've paused the rule and revoked the account. Pulling full audit trail; adding SRE and SecOps to thread.

Maya Singh (SecOps) 2026-03-13T10:05:03Z: Forensics pulled the DOCX. Appears the token is base64 and wrapped in an HTML comment inside the docx XML. No evidence yet of exfil prior to provisioning. Collecting file hashes and vendor metadata.
Evan Brooks (SRE) 2026-03-13T10:22:45Z: Noted a spike of 3 provisioning events matching the same matcher in the last 48 hours. Correlating with partner uploads from vendor-8923 IP range.

Jordan Kim 2026-03-13T14:01:00Z: Adding mitigation plan: input sanitization on ingest-service, stricter matching, and require operator approval for any rule-triggered IAM provisioning. Draft PR ready.

Maya Singh 2026-03-14T08:15:00Z: Confirmed no lateral movement. File contains a JWT with a claim set pointing to an external URL; token signature uses HMAC with leaked shared key (rotated now). Recommend forcing rotation across other automations using same matcher.
investigation_notes: 09:45: Evidence: DOCX internal XML showed <!--TOKEN: eyJhbGciOiJI...--> inside word/document.xml. The ingest parser treats HTML comments as safe text and included in metadata extraction.
11:10: Hypothesis: An attacker embedded tokens in commonly uploaded docs. The provisioning matcher did not validate token origin or require operator confirmation for high-cost actions.

12:30: Confirmed two other vendor uploads from same vendor account earlier this week that contained similarly structured payloads but didn't match the exact regex; we patched regex to be more conservative.
15:00: Correlated provisioning IP 18.215.42.33 to a CI runner previously associated with vendor-8923; vendor outreach initiated to confirm intent.

Next steps: complete PR to require human approval for IAM provisioning; add a sanitization step to strip tokens from extracted text; run a retrospective search for other docs containing 'TOKEN:' pattern across partner buckets.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: automation rule disabled, service-account revoked, signing keys rotated, vendor contacted for explanation. Longer-term controls in progress: input sanitization in ingest-service (PR ready), operator-approval gating for IAM provisioning, monitoring rule to alert on token-like patterns in uploaded artifacts. Ticket will remain open until PR is merged and retrospective search completes.
follow_up_tasks: SEC-1: Merge PR to add sanitization and stricter matching to ingest-service (assigned to infra-team)
SEC-2: Implement operator approval flow in iam-provisioner for rule-based provisioning (assigned to iam-team)
SEC-3: Run retrospective scan across partners-ingest-prod for token-like patterns and report findings (assigned to SecOps)
SEC-4: Vendor outreach complete: get signed attestation from vendor-8923 and rotate their partner API keys if necessary
